name: Champa Shashti Jatre (Champa Shashti Mahotsava)
what: The biggest fortnight of the year at Kukke: nightly vahana processions, a Laksha Deepotsava on 8 Dec, the flower chariot on 13 Dec, the Panchami rathotsava on the night of 14 Dec and the Champa Shashti Maharathotsava early on 15 Dec. Avabhritha and the boat procession follow on 16 Dec, and the koppari is lowered on 21 Dec.
tips: If you only go once, go for the night of 14 Dec and stay for the morning chariot on 15 Dec; expect very large crowds and book rooms early or day-trip. The schedule was published by the temple administration on 22 Nov 2026 (reported by V4 News). Dress code and annadana meal timings during the jatre: verify locally. Approach roads are hilly and get jammed; avoid riding back at night after the rathotsava.

name: Champa Shashti Maharathotsava (main chariot day)
what: The main Brahmarathotsava of the year: the big chariot is pulled at dawn on Margashira Shukla Shashti, after the Panchami chariot the night before. Drik Panchang (set to Mangaluru) also puts Subrahmanya Shashti on Tue 15 Dec 2026.
tips: Be in position before first light; the chariot runs in the early morning (pratahkala). Crowds are at their peak, so leave the bike at a lot on the edge of town and walk. Verify dress code and the day's darshan and annadana timings locally.

name: Kiru Shashti Mahotsava
what: The "small Shashti", a smaller follow-up festival at Kukke a month after Champa Shashti. Far thinner crowds than December, so it suits a calmer visit.
tips: The date is from the temple's jatre announcement; programme details were not published with it, so check timings locally. It falls right before Makara Sankranti, so roads to the coast may be busy.

name: Laksha Deepotsava
what: Five nights of lamps at the end of Karthika, with a different utsava each night: Kere Katte (5 Dec), Lalitodyana (6 Dec), Kanchimaru Katte (7 Dec) and Gaurimaru Katte (8 Dec), plus a state-level exhibition from 4 Dec. The Sarva Dharma Sammelana is on 7 Dec and the Sahitya Sammelana on 8 Dec, both at 5 pm in the Amrutavarshini hall.
tips: The lamp-lit processions are after dark, so plan to stay overnight rather than ride back late on dark roads. Evening cultural programmes run roughly 5.30 pm to 11.30 pm on the exhibition stage. Last night (8 Dec) is the busiest. Annadana and dress-code details for the festival days: verify locally. The Jain Samavasarana puja follows on 9 Dec.

name: Yakshagana touring (tirugata) season
what: About 45 Badagutittu and Tenkutittu melas are touring this season, setting up stages in temple yards and paddy fields almost every night. Start dates reported for 2026-27: Kamalashile 10 Nov, Saligrama 12 Nov, Mandarthi (5 melas) and Maranakatte 18 Nov, Perduru 20 Nov, Dharmasthala tour 29 Nov, all seven Kateel melas and Kukke 3 Dec.
tips: Many shows are now time-limited, but some organisers still book all-night shows; ask the start time. The season traditionally ends at Pattanaje (late May); the exact 2027 end date was not announced. Most shows are free seva-ata sponsored by devotees: ask at the temple office or local shops where the mela is playing that night. Carry a shawl for the cold early hours and avoid riding back after midnight.

name: Kateel Yakshagana melas begin their tour
what: All seven Kateel Sri Durgaparameshwari melas start their annual tour on the same day, the biggest single troupe roster on the coast. After this, a Kateel mela is playing somewhere in Dakshina Kannada most nights until the season ends.
tips: The opening performances are traditionally at the kshetra itself, but where each mela plays on a given night changes daily; check locally. Tenkutittu style, so expect a different costume and drumming style from the Badagutittu melas closer to Manipal.

name: Dharmasthala Yakshagana mela tour
what: The Dharmasthala mela starts touring on 29 Nov; it has been doing seva performances at the kshetra since 12 Nov. Worth combining with a Laksha Deepotsava trip in the first week of December.
tips: Nightly venue changes; check at the temple. Shows at the kshetra itself are the easiest to catch.

name: Kakkepadavu Kambala
what: Pairs of buffaloes thunder down a flooded paddy track while a barefoot jockey hangs on behind, and the whole village turns out to shout them home. Kakkepadavu is on the State Kambala Association's revised 2026-27 calendar for 2026-11-28.
tips: Races start on the listed day and, by State Kambala Association rules, must finish within 24 hours (up to 150 pairs) or 30 hours (more than 150 pairs), so the best runs often come late at night or the next morning. Wear shoes you do not mind getting muddy and stand well back from the track edge where the buffaloes come in. Riding home after an all-night race is a bad idea: plan to leave in daylight. Food stalls are common at kambala grounds but veg options vary, so eat before you go. Dates come from the association's revised list; organisers sometimes shift them, so check the week before.

name: Vaikuntha Ekadashi (with Gita Jayanti)
place: Vishnu and Krishna temples across the coast, incl. Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
what: The Ekadashi of Margashira Shukla, when Vishnu temples hold special darshan and many devotees fast. Drik Panchang set to Mangaluru gives Sun 20 Dec 2026, the same day as Gita Jayanti and Mokshada Ekadashi.
tips: Some Smarta and Vaishnava calendars differ by a day, so check what your temple observes. Udupi-specific programmes for the day were not found: verify locally. Fasting food (no grains) is the norm for those observing.

name: Hanuman Jayanti (Hanumad Vrata, Karnataka)
place: Hanuman and Mukhyaprana shrines across the region
what: Karnataka marks Hanuman Jayanti on Margashira Shukla Trayodashi, not in April as up north. Drik Panchang's Kannada calendar set to Mangaluru gives Tue 22 Dec 2026.
tips: No specific coastal temple programme was found; ask at Mukhyaprana shrines (including the one at Udupi Krishna Matha) for timings.

name: Datta Jayanti
what: The birth of Dattatreya on Margashira Purnima. Drik Panchang set to Mangaluru gives Wed 23 Dec 2026.
tips: No specific coastal Karnataka venue was verified; check locally.

name: Christmas in Mangaluru
place: Mangaluru churches (Rosario Cathedral, Milagres and others)
what: Mangaluru's big Catholic community makes Christmas a citywide event: carols and midnight masses on the 24th, and in past years thousands at Rosario Cathedral, Milagres, Urwa, Bejai and Bondel. Parishes build elaborate cribs for weeks, and crib-hopping draws people of every faith.
tips: Mass timings for 2026 were not published yet; check the parish or Diocese of Mangalore notices. Be respectful at services. Christmas sweets (kuswar) are a Mangalorean Catholic tradition; some recipes use egg, so ask before eating.

name: Makara Sankranti
place: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha and temples across the coast
what: Drik Panchang gives Makara Sankranti 2027 as Fri 15 Jan (the sun enters Makara late on 14 Jan, so the observance moves to the 15th). At Udupi, Sankranti is the sixth day of Saptotsava and brings the first Brahmarathotsava of the year.
tips: Some calendars still list 14 Jan; confirm with the Matha which night the Brahmaratha runs. Kadri Manjunatha's annual jatre also traditionally starts around Sankranti.

name: Saptotsava and Makara Sankranti Brahmarathotsava
what: Seven days of night chariot processions around the Car Street: two chariots on the first five nights, the Brahma Ratha with Krishna on Sankranti (day six), and Choornotsava by day on the seventh. In 2025 it ran 9 to 15 Jan; 2027 is the first Saptotsava of the Shiroor Matha Paryaya (2026-28).
tips: If Sankranti is 15 Jan 2027, Saptotsava would run roughly 10 to 16 Jan, but the Matha had not announced dates: confirm locally. Car Street gets packed after dark; park at the edge of town. Dress code inside the Matha: verify the current rule at the gate. Prasada meal arrangements during Saptotsava: verify locally.

name: Kadri Manjunatha annual jatre and rathotsava
what: A roughly ten-day festival that traditionally opens on Makara Sankranti, ending with the chariot pulled round the temple streets. Past schedules: 15 to 25 Jan in 2020, and 14 to 24 Jan 2026 with the rathotsava on 21 Jan.
tips: 2027 dates not yet published; expect mid to late January. The rathotsava evening is the busiest.

name: Guru Narasimha car festival (Ratharohana)
what: Saligrama's Guru Narasimha temple pulls its chariot in Makara masa, around Uttarayana Sankranti; Wikipedia cites 16 Jan.
tips: No 2027 date was published; ask at the temple. Pair it with an evening show by the Saligrama Yakshagana mela, which started its tour on 12 Nov.

name: Kodi Habba (Brahmarathotsava)
what: Kundapura's biggest fair, where a bamboo chariot is pulled and newly married couples carry home sugarcane. It falls on the full moon of the solar month Vrischika; past dates were 27 Nov 2023, 15 Dec 2024 and 4 to 5 Dec 2025.
tips: No 2026 date was found. By the Vrischika full-moon rule it may fall around 24 Nov 2026, before your window: phone the temple (listed as 08254262230 on utsav.gov.in) to check.

name: Karavali Utsav (Mangaluru)
what: The Dakshina Kannada district's winter festival of beach events, cultural nights and food stalls. On 2 Nov 2026 U.T. Khader asked officials to plan it for December; dates and venues were not yet announced.
tips: Last edition ran 20 Dec 2025 to 4 Jan 2026 (stalls extended later). Planned extras this year include a triathlon, vintage car rally and helicopter rides. Food stalls include a seafood festival; stick to the veg counters.

name: Karavali Utsav (Karwar)
what: Uttara Kannada's own Karavali Utsav, held on Rabindranath Tagore Beach. The 2025 edition was scheduled for 22 to 28 Dec 2025; no 2026 dates were found.
tips: Karwar is a long ride or a Konkan Railway trip from Udupi; only plan around it once the district announces dates.
